When confronting these results with the mental health outcomes, we show that the more socially desirable cluster exhibited a higher score on positive aspects such as life satisfaction and purpose in life. In the functional brain connectivity, we observe that the cluster with a more socially beneficial profile exhibits lower interconnectivity, especially in the default mode network. The pipeline we present uses a combined analysis of both fMRI and psychosocial variables, which could open the path for more extensive analysis.
tldr: This paper studies the relationship between psychosocial profiles, mental health, and brain functional connectivity using survey data and resting-state fMRI from the Human Connectome Project.
motivation: To understand how personality traits (inner self) and social support (outer self) are related and how they reflect in brain networks and mental health outcomes.
method: Correlation analysis of z-score standardized survey measures and k-means clustering to group individuals by social profiles, followed by comparison of mental health outcomes and functional brain connectivity between clusters.
result: Social indicators group more by impact on social experience than by inner/outer self; the socially desirable cluster shows higher life satisfaction and lower default mode network interconnectivity.
conclusion: The combined analysis of fMRI and psychosocial variables can reveal links between social profiles, mental health, and brain connectivity, opening avenues for further research.

title: On The Stability Of Scale-space Metrics
authors: William Leeb
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stability of a classical family of metrics defined over functions' Gaussian scale-space representations, focusing on the comparison of images (functions of two variables). These metrics have precedents both in harmonic analysis, specifically the theory of Besov spaces, and in classical methods of image processing; special cases are also known to be metrically equivalent to certain Wasserstein distances. We quantify these metrics' robustness to geometric deformations, and introduce rotationally-invariant versions that are stable to changes in angle when comparing tomographic projections. We also describe computationally efficient algorithms for evaluating the metrics from finite samples, and prove their robustness to additive noise. The results are illustrated through numerical experiments.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of scale-space metrics for image comparison, with connections to Besov spaces and Wasserstein distances.
motivation: To quantify robustness of image metrics to geometric deformations and noise, and to develop rotationally-invariant versions for tomographic projections.
method: Theoretical analysis of metric stability under deformations and noise, plus computational algorithms for finite-sample evaluation.
result: Proved stability bounds and introduced rotationally-invariant metrics; demonstrated robustness numerically.
conclusion: Scale-space metrics are stable and computationally feasible for image comparison tasks.

title: Geometry-Preserving Reduced-Order Modeling Via Immersed Tensor Decomposition (itd)
authors: Lei Zhang, Jiachen Guo, Guowei He, Thomas J. R. Hughes, Wing Kam Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Body-fitted finite-element methods deliver high-order accuracy but hinge on a clean, watertight, conforming mesh, a requirement that breaks down for the geometrically imperfect CAD assemblies, image-based volumetric data, and voxel-native designs that pervade biomedical engineering and additive manufacturing, where mesh generation has become the dominant cost of the analysis cycle. Immersed methods on regular background Cartesian grids sidestep body-fitted meshing, but classical implementations integrate over irregular cut subdomains, destroying the tensor-product structure that enables separable, reduced-order methods such as tensor decomposition. In this paper we propose the (ITD) framework, which couples a mesh-free geometric representation via body-fitted function with the separable C-HiDeNN-TD reduced-order solver to enable large-scale simulation directly on regular background voxel meshes. The geometry is encoded in three steps: a signed-distance function represents the boundary, a body-fitted function [MATH] approximates it with controllable error, and a low-rank Tucker decomposition provides model-order reduction; for a fixed grid spacing [MATH], accuracy is improved by raising the approximation order of C-HiDeNN interpolation up to degree [MATH] with a linear background mesh. The central contribution is an exact Dirichlet formulation that enforces the boundary condition strongly by multiplying the trial function with [MATH], so that [MATH] holds by construction without any variational penalty or interface quadrature. We establish an a priori error estimate for the formulation and assess it on canonical 2D/3D domains, demonstrating optimal convergence and robustness on non-Cartesian geometries discretized by regular voxel meshes.
tldr: A reduced-order modeling framework for immersed finite-element methods on regular Cartesian grids, using tensor decomposition and body-fitted functions to handle complex geometries without conforming meshes.
motivation: Body-fitted meshing is a bottleneck for complex geometries from CAD, imaging, and additive manufacturing; immersed methods on Cartesian grids avoid meshing but lose tensor-product structure needed for efficient reduced-order models.
method: The ITD framework combines a signed-distance function for geometry, a body-fitted function for approximation, and low-rank Tucker decomposition for model-order reduction, with an exact Dirichlet formulation that enforces boundary conditions strongly via multiplication.
result: A priori error estimates are established, and numerical tests on 2D/3D domains show optimal convergence and robustness on non-Cartesian geometries discretized by regular voxel meshes.
conclusion: The ITD framework enables large-scale simulation directly on regular background voxel meshes without body-fitted meshing, preserving accuracy and tensor-product efficiency.

title: Analysis, Thermodynamics, And A Numeric Solver For A Pressure-temperature Equilibrium Closure Of The Four-equation Model
authors: Bennett Clayton, Joshua Mcconnell, Clell Solomon
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze an often used closure model for multi-material hydrodynamics where pressure temperature equilibrium (PTE) is assumed for every state; emphasis is placed on tabular equations of state. This multi-material model is often referred to as the four-equation model. The identification of the admissible set is presented and is proven to be convex, setting the foundation for development of invariant-domain methods for this model. A novel, robust, and efficient method is presented for solving the highly nonlinear system for the equilibrated pressure and temperature with an arbitrary number of materials. Additionally, we provide a detailed analysis of the thermodynamics of the mixture model for general equations of state and prove existence and uniqueness of the pressure-temperature equilibrium solution under some thermodynamic assumptions.
tldr: This paper analyzes a pressure-temperature equilibrium closure for multi-material hydrodynamics, focusing on numerical methods and thermodynamic existence proofs.
motivation: To provide a rigorous mathematical foundation for the four-equation model used in multi-material hydrodynamics, ensuring robust numerical methods.
method: The authors identify the admissible set, prove its convexity, and develop a novel solver for the nonlinear pressure-temperature equilibrium system with tabular equations of state.
result: Existence and uniqueness of the pressure-temperature equilibrium solution are proven under thermodynamic assumptions, and a robust solver is presented.
conclusion: The work establishes a theoretical basis for invariant-domain methods in multi-material hydrodynamics, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics of computation, or quantum systems.

title: Zonal Spherical Functions Of Quantum Symmetric Pairs
authors: Philip Schl\"osser
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We identify the zonal and character spherical functions for quantum symmetric pairs with the symmetric Koornwinder--Macdonald polynomials. To this end, the methods of Letzter's 2004 paper are translated to modern conventions and right coideal subalgebras, and extended to non-standard cases and cases with non-reduced restricted root systems. For the last elusive Satake type, FII, a conjecture is provided.
tldr: The paper identifies zonal spherical functions for quantum symmetric pairs with symmetric Koornwinder–Macdonald polynomials, extending Letzter's methods to non-standard cases.
motivation: To understand the representation theory of quantum symmetric pairs and connect it to special functions.
method: Translates Letzter's 2004 methods to modern conventions and right coideal subalgebras, extending to non-standard and non-reduced root systems.
result: Zonal and character spherical functions are identified with symmetric Koornwinder–Macdonald polynomials, with a conjecture for the FII Satake type.
conclusion: The work provides a unified framework for spherical functions in quantum symmetric spaces, linking to known orthogonal polynomials.

title: Computing Accurate Singular Vectors And Eigenvectors Using Mixed-precision Jacobi Algorithms
authors: Zhengbo Zhou, Fran\c{c}oise Tisseur, Marcus Webb
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mixed-precision variants of the Jacobi algorithm for symmetric positive definite eigenproblems and the one-sided Jacobi algorithm for singular value decompositions have recently been shown to compute eigenvalues and singular values to high relative accuracy. However, these analyses do not address the accuracy of the computed eigenvectors and singular vectors. In this paper, we prove error bounds for the computed eigenvectors and singular vectors, where the error is measured by the sine of the angle between the vector and its computed counterpart. The obtained bounds preserve the relative gap structure of the bounds for Jacobi algorithms proved by Demmel and Veseli\'{c}, but involve the scaled condition number of the preconditioned matrix rather than that of the original matrix (the former of which is typically much smaller). Numerical experiments support our theoretical bounds and demonstrate that the mixed-precision preconditioned Jacobi algorithms are especially effective for ill-conditioned matrices with small absolute gaps and moderate relative gaps between eigenvalues or singular values.
tldr: This paper proves error bounds for eigenvectors and singular vectors computed by mixed-precision Jacobi algorithms, focusing on numerical linear algebra rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Previous work showed mixed-precision Jacobi algorithms compute eigenvalues and singular values accurately, but accuracy of eigenvectors and singular vectors was unaddressed.
method: The authors derive error bounds measured by the sine of the angle between computed and true vectors, using the scaled condition number of the preconditioned matrix.
result: The bounds preserve the relative gap structure from Demmel and Veselić but involve a smaller condition number, and numerical experiments confirm effectiveness for ill-conditioned matrices.
conclusion: Mixed-precision preconditioned Jacobi algorithms compute eigenvectors and singular vectors accurately, especially for matrices with small absolute gaps and moderate relative gaps.

title: Reservoir Zero-Coordinatewise Projected Subspace Search For Minimization Over Sparse Symmetric Sets In Machine Learning
authors: Morteza Kimiaei, Shima Shabani, Michael Breuss
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a class of nonconvex cardinality-constrained optimization problems arising in sparse learning. These problems are NP-hard due to the combinatorial nature of sparsity constraints. We introduce a Reservoir Zero-Coordinatewise Projected Subspace Search (RZCW-PSS) algorithm, a simplex-style method on sparse manifolds that integrates coordinatewise search, symmetry-aware swap-based support updates, randomized low-dimensional subspace exploration, and zero-coordinatewise reservoir injection. The proposed method augments classical coordinate and swap moves with sparse-compatible subspace searches constructed from a dynamically maintained reservoir of previously accepted feasible points. A key feature of the approach is a refined reservoir initialization strategy that embeds sparse projection directly into a uniform sampling procedure, preserving geometric diversity within the feasible set. The algorithm also includes an optional support-identification safeguard that enforces full-support stabilization under a fixed support-change decrease threshold. We establish that, under the stated regularity, sampling, and subproblem-accuracy assumptions, every full-support accumulation point of the RZCW-PSS iterates is Beck--Hallak zero-coordinatewise stationary almost surely; with the safeguard and full-support initialization, this conclusion applies to all accumulation points. We further prove a conditional local linear convergence rate after support stabilization and derive the corresponding logarithmic local iteration complexity. Numerical experiments on synthetic sparse learning problems demonstrate that RZCW-PSS improves robustness and solution quality while remaining computationally competitive with Partial Simplex Search, Basic Feasible Search, and Zero-Coordinatewise Search methods.
tldr: This paper proposes a new algorithm for cardinality-constrained optimization in sparse learning, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Sparse learning problems are NP-hard due to combinatorial sparsity constraints, and existing methods may lack robustness or efficiency.
method: The Reservoir Zero-Coordinatewise Projected Subspace Search (RZCW-PSS) algorithm combines coordinatewise search, swap-based support updates, randomized subspace exploration, and a reservoir of feasible points.
result: The algorithm achieves zero-coordinatewise stationarity almost surely under regularity conditions and demonstrates improved robustness and solution quality on synthetic problems.
conclusion: RZCW-PSS is a competitive method for sparse optimization, but it is purely in the domain of machine learning and optimization, unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Commutative Topological Algebras On Translation-invariant Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Spaces
authors: Miguel Angel Rodriguez Rodriguez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study commutative topological algebras naturally associated with translation-invariant reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces whose direct integral decomposition has one-dimensional fibers. Starting from the bounded algebra of translation-invariant operators, we pass to a common dense domain generated by reproducing kernels and identify the corresponding diagonalizable operators with multiplication by symbols in an intersection of weighted [MATH]-spaces. On the symbol side this gives a canonical space [MATH] and a maximal multiplicative subalgebra [MATH], which is a complete locally convex [MATH]-algebra. Transporting the structure back yields corresponding algebras of operators and integral kernels. We also discuss when the inclusions [MATH] are strict, and illustrate the results with vertical and radial operators on classical Bergman and Fock spaces.
tldr: This paper studies commutative topological algebras on translation-invariant reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces, focusing on operator algebras and symbol spaces.
motivation: To understand the algebraic structure of operators on certain function spaces and their diagonalization.
method: Uses direct integral decomposition and constructs dense domains from reproducing kernels to identify diagonalizable operators with multiplication operators.
result: Defines a canonical symbol space and a maximal multiplicative subalgebra, and discusses strictness of inclusions.
conclusion: Provides a framework for commutative algebras of operators on translation-invariant RKHS, with examples on Bergman and Fock spaces.

title: Second-Order Kkt Guarantees For Bregman Admm In Nonconvex And Non-Lipschitz Optimization
authors: Shuang Li, Zhihui Zhu, Qiuwei Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28307v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze Bregman ADMM for nonconvex linearly constrained problems under two-sided relative smoothness, a condition that replaces the standard Lipschitz gradient assumption with a Hessian comparison relative to a Bregman kernel. This setting covers polynomial objectives arising in matrix and tensor models for which a global Lipschitz-gradient constant need not exist. We show that on an invariant open state-space domain, one iteration of Bregman ADMM defines a smooth primal--dual fixed-point map whose strict-saddle KKT points are unstable fixed points; consequently, from random initialization the iterates converge to a strict saddle with probability zero. Combined with existing first-order convergence results, this yields almost-sure second-order stationarity of limiting KKT points. We extend the analysis to a multi-block star consensus formulation for distributed optimization. The technical novelty lies in a determinant reduction with a Bregman-specific symmetrization and scaling step in the two block spectral argument, together with a null space cancellation exploiting the star graph structure in the consensus case. Numerical experiments on distributed matrix factorization illustrate the theory, and a symmetric tensor factorization example demonstrates the broader Bregman proximal splitting idea beyond the separable consensus setting.
tldr: This paper provides second-order KKT guarantees for Bregman ADMM in nonconvex and non-Lipschitz optimization, focusing on matrix and tensor factorization.
motivation: Standard Lipschitz gradient assumptions fail for polynomial objectives in matrix/tensor models; the authors aim to prove convergence to second-order stationary points under weaker conditions.
method: They analyze Bregman ADMM under two-sided relative smoothness, using a determinant reduction with Bregman-specific symmetrization and a null space cancellation for star consensus.
result: They show that strict-saddle KKT points are unstable fixed points, so from random initialization iterates converge to a strict saddle with probability zero, ensuring almost-sure second-order stationarity.
conclusion: Bregman ADMM can guarantee second-order optimality for nonconvex problems without Lipschitz gradients, with applications to distributed matrix factorization and symmetric tensor factorization.

title: Tropical Fermat--Weber Problems Over Non-Finite Data And Their Inverse Formulations
authors: Ruriko Yoshida John Sabol
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The term tropical pseudonorm refers to a family of (not necessarily symmetric) gauge functions that arise in tropical or idempotent geometry. An important characteristic of these gauges is their invariance under translation by a constant vector, allowing them to descent naturally to tropical projective spaces. In this work, we explore the tropical one-infinity pseudonorm, a polyhedral hybrid gauge that allows for tunable asymmetry, in the context of a Fermat--Weber location problem. We extend previous formulations in considering non-finite data, and we investigate several variants of the inverse problem, providing linear programming formulations for their solution.
tldr: This paper studies tropical Fermat-Weber problems with non-finite data and their inverse formulations using linear programming.
motivation: To extend tropical location theory to handle data points at infinity and to solve inverse problems that recover parameters from given solutions.
method: The authors define the tropical one-infinity pseudonorm and formulate the Fermat-Weber problem as a linear program, then derive inverse variants also solvable via linear programming.
result: They provide linear programming formulations for both forward and inverse tropical Fermat-Weber problems with non-finite data.
conclusion: The work advances tropical geometry applications in location analysis but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Provable Reductions In Tfnp
authors: Noah Fleming, Stefan Grosser, Toniann Pitassi, Robert Robere
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new family of propositional proof systems, denoted , for an arbitrary TFNP search problem [MATH]. Informally, a refutation of a CNF formula [MATH] in is given by a polynomial-time reduction from the false-clause search problem [MATH] to [MATH], combined with an Extended Frege proof that the reduction is correct. These are motivated in two ways: 1. They are the propositional translations of witnessing theorems in bounded arithmetic, by which proofs of [MATH] formulas [MATH] in a theory [MATH] imply algorithms solving the search problem for [MATH] in a TFNP class corresponding to [MATH]. 2. They are a white-box analogue of the characterizations of proof systems using decision tree reductions to black-box TFNP problems. We consider the proof system , where Iter is a complete problem for PLS. We prove that is polynomially equivalent to the sequent calculus [MATH], and also to the implicit Resolution proof system [EF, Resolution]. Hence [MATH] and [EF, Resolution] are equivalent, which is the first characterization of an implicit proof system by a classical proof system beyond the work of Wang. We also consider for general TFNP relations [MATH]. We observe that if EF can prove that a search problem [MATH] is in FP, then is polynomially equivalent to EF. This contrasts to our above result, which shows that Extended-Frege provable reductions to [MATH], a problem widely believed not to be in FP, yields a proof system ([MATH]) that is believed to be stronger than Extended Frege. Finally, we show that for any proof system [MATH] which is sufficiently strong, there is a polynomial-time computable search problem [MATH] FP such that is polynomially equivalent to [MATH]. Letting [MATH] [EF, Resolution] and combining our two results shows that is polynomially equivalent to .
tldr: This paper introduces a new family of propositional proof systems based on TFNP search problems and studies their equivalence to classical proof systems.
motivation: To connect TFNP search problems with propositional proof complexity and to characterize implicit proof systems via classical ones.
method: Defines proof systems where refutations are polynomial-time reductions from false-clause search to a TFNP problem, combined with Extended Frege proofs of correctness; analyzes equivalences with sequent calculus and implicit Resolution.
result: Proves that the proof system based on the PLS-complete problem Iter is polynomially equivalent to the sequent calculus G and to implicit Resolution, and shows general equivalences for other TFNP problems.
conclusion: The work provides new connections between TFNP, bounded arithmetic, and proof complexity, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: What Was That Again? Certified Robustness For Automatic Speech Recognition
authors: Andrew C. Cullen, Neil Marchant, Jiani Xie, Paul Montague, Benjamin I. P. Rubinstein
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27698v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition systems are notoriously both sensitive to adversarial and benign perturbations. While this has been repeatedly demonstrated using reference datasets, detecting such behaviors in deployed systems is incredibly challenging, due to the absence of oracle knowledge of the true transcription. We demonstrate that employing a certification-inspired mechanism can significantly decrease WER, increase recall, and decrease the Spearman correlation between confidence and WER. We achieve this through a dual-gate diagnostic pipeline: a Two-Sided Atomic Audit that accumulates statistical wealth to certify both token existence and adversarial exclusion, and a Rank-Based Tournament that selects the winning sequence. Our evaluations across four diverse architectures demonstrate up to a 55% relative reduction in Word Error Rate, while also providing granular word- and sentence-level certifications to enhance acoustic security.
tldr: This paper proposes a certification-inspired method to improve robustness of automatic speech recognition systems against adversarial and benign perturbations.
motivation: Automatic speech recognition systems are sensitive to perturbations, but detecting such behaviors in deployed systems is challenging due to lack of oracle knowledge of true transcription.
method: A dual-gate diagnostic pipeline consisting of a Two-Sided Atomic Audit for statistical certification and a Rank-Based Tournament for sequence selection.
result: Achieves up to 55% relative reduction in Word Error Rate across four diverse architectures, with granular word- and sentence-level certifications.
conclusion: The proposed method enhances acoustic security and robustness of ASR systems without requiring oracle knowledge.

title: Co-Optimization Of Analog Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks For Low-Power Function Approximation In Flexible Electronics
authors: Paula Carolina Lozano Duarte, Georgios Zervakis, Mehdi Tahoori, Sani Nassif
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Wearable devices and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors require on-sensor processing of biosignals and environmental data, including computationally demanding operations such as nonlinear activation functions for neural network inference, sensor calibration curves to map raw readings to physical units, and signal preprocessing functions like logarithmic compression and power operations for feature extraction. These functions exhibit significant complexity, often involving transcendental operations and multivariate dependencies that are costly to implement digitally. Analog function approximation provides a power-efficient alternative by performing these computations in the analog domain, thereby reducing the energy overhead associated with analog-to-digital conversion and subsequent digital processing. Flexible Electronics (FE) present a particularly attractive platform for wearable applications due to mechanical flexibility and low-cost fabrication, but impose strict constraints on circuit density and power consumption, making efficient analog implementations critical but challenging. This work introduces Analog Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (AKANs), developed via hardware-software co-optimization, to approximate these complex multivariate functions accurately under hardware imperfections. Our method incorporates circuit-level error modeling during training and applies pruning at both software and hardware levels to reduce area and power. Validation across multiple benchmarks demonstrates that our proposed pruning methodology not only reduces hardware cost but can also improve approximation accuracy by regularizing spline parameters. Results show up to 55% area and 50% power savings, with average reductions of nearly 30% across datasets, highlighting AKANs as a robust and generalizable framework for low-power analog function approximation in FE.
tldr: This paper presents a hardware-software co-optimization framework for analog Kolmogorov-Arnold networks to approximate complex functions in low-power flexible electronics.
motivation: Wearable and IoT devices require energy-efficient on-sensor processing of nonlinear functions, which are costly to implement digitally. Flexible electronics impose strict area and power constraints, motivating analog function approximation.
method: The authors propose Analog Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (AKANs) with circuit-level error modeling during training and pruning at both software and hardware levels to reduce area and power.
result: The method achieves up to 55% area and 50% power savings with average reductions of nearly 30% across benchmarks, and pruning can improve approximation accuracy by regularizing spline parameters.
conclusion: AKANs provide a robust and generalizable framework for low-power analog function approximation in flexible electronics, suitable for wearable and IoT applications.

title: Transversal Difference Numbers In Finite Abelian Quotients
authors: Mugurel Barcau, Vicen\c{t}iu Pa\c{s}ol, George C. \c{t}urca\c{s}
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27961v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given \(H\leq G\) finite abelian groups, a transversal \(T\subseteq G\) for \(G/H\) has fixed size \(|G/H|\), but its ambient difference support \(D(T)=T-T\) can vary with the embedding of \(H\) in \(G\). We call [MATH] the transversal difference number of the pair \((G,H)\). This invariant is related to finite abelian factorisation, tiling complements, and small-sumset questions, and is motivated by recent work regarding ambient Galois labels in CRT transforms for cyclotomic-subfield homomorphic encryption. We prove various results regarding this invariant, including a general lower bound [MATH] where \(m(G,H)\) is the largest order of a subgroup of \(G\) disjoint from \(H\). The bound is sharp for cyclic quotients, and Kneser's theorem gives a cross-transversal estimate leading to exact product families with one nonsplit cyclic coordinate and arbitrary split factors. These results isolate the first genuinely new residual obstruction, namely the same-prime square plane \[ G=(\mathbb Z/p^2\mathbb Z)^2,\qquad H=pG. \] For odd \(p\), this case is the technical core of the paper. Here transversals are graphs of functions \(\mathbb F_p^2\to \mathbb F_p^2\), and \(D(T)\) decomposes into carry-corrected finite-field derivative images. We conjecture that \[ \delta(G,H)=(2p-1)^2 \] for all odd primes \(p\), prove the unconditional lower bound \(3p^2-p-1\), and give small-prime, probabilistic, and fixed-polynomial evidence for the conjecture.
tldr: The paper studies transversal difference numbers in finite abelian groups, an invariant related to factorization and tiling, motivated by homomorphic encryption.
motivation: To understand how the difference set of a transversal varies with the embedding of a subgroup, with applications to CRT-based homomorphic encryption.
method: Uses combinatorial and group-theoretic arguments, including Kneser's theorem, to derive lower bounds and exact formulas for specific group pairs.
result: Proves a general lower bound involving the largest order of a subgroup disjoint from H, and gives exact results for product families; identifies a critical case (Z/p^2Z)^2 with H=pG and provides evidence for a conjectured value.
conclusion: The invariant isolates a new obstruction in abelian group factorization, with the square plane case being the technical core.

title: AI-Driven Synthesis For High-Tech System Design: Automating Innovation
authors: Luuk Oerlemans, Steven Westerhof, Theo Hofman
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28126v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article addresses the combinatorial complexity inherent in modern high-tech system design by presenting automation-in-design (AiD) as a transformative paradigm. We propose computational design synthesis (CDS), a framework utilising deep learning and generative AI to automate the creation of novel systems. Two case studies (e-drive system design and spatial dimensioning problem) serve as proof-points for this approach. The AI-driven methods used in the case studies represent a fundamental shift in engineering, advancing from simulation-based optimisation towards autonomous design with minimal human supervision.
tldr: This paper presents an AI-driven computational design synthesis framework for automating high-tech system design, with case studies in e-drive and spatial dimensioning.
motivation: Modern high-tech system design faces combinatorial complexity that traditional simulation-based optimization cannot handle efficiently.
method: The authors propose a computational design synthesis (CDS) framework using deep learning and generative AI to automate the creation of novel systems, demonstrated through two case studies.
result: The AI-driven methods enable autonomous design with minimal human supervision, advancing from simulation-based optimization to automated synthesis.
conclusion: The approach represents a paradigm shift in engineering design, but the paper focuses on classical engineering automation rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Extracting Behavioural Properties From Face-to-face Interactions Temporal Networks: A Measure Of Egonet Persistency
authors: Gabriel Maurial, Elisa Kl\"uger, Mathieu G\'enois
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding how individuals repeat social interactions over time is a central problem in the analysis of temporal networks. In social systems, repeated interactions shape processes such as information diffusion, collective coordination, and the emergence of social structure. Existing measures of egonet persistence often conflate genuine behavioural regularities with structural effects such as node degree, making it difficult to distinguish meaningful temporal correlations from random mixing. In this work, we introduce the Neighbourhood Persistency Criterion (NPC), a statistically grounded framework for quantifying egonet persistence across time. NPC combines classical similarity measures with tailored null models controlling for network topology and interaction weights. We apply this framework to high temporal resolution face-to-face interaction networks collected at four Computational Social Science conferences using the SocioPatterns platform. Our results reveal a common behavioural structure across events, characterised by an exploration[MATH]exploitation trade-off in social interactions. While many individuals alternate between both strategies, others exhibit stable interaction patterns throughout the event. Importantly, these behaviours show little systematic association with socio-demographic attributes, suggesting that interaction strategies are shaped primarily by contextual factors rather than stable individual traits. NPC thus provides a flexible and interpretable tool for studying egonet persistence in temporal networks and social systems.
tldr: This paper introduces a statistical framework to quantify egonet persistence in face-to-face interaction temporal networks, revealing exploration-exploitation trade-offs in social behavior.
motivation: Existing measures of egonet persistence conflate genuine behavioral regularities with structural effects like node degree, making it hard to distinguish meaningful temporal correlations from random mixing.
method: The authors propose the Neighbourhood Persistency Criterion (NPC), which combines classical similarity measures with tailored null models controlling for network topology and interaction weights, and apply it to high-resolution face-to-face interaction data from four conferences.
result: The analysis reveals a common exploration-exploitation trade-off across events, with some individuals alternating strategies and others showing stable patterns, and little association with socio-demographic attributes.
conclusion: NPC provides a flexible and interpretable tool for studying egonet persistence, suggesting that interaction strategies are shaped primarily by contextual factors rather than stable individual traits.

title: Preferentiality And Bandwidth Drive Tie Activity In Online And Offline Ego Networks
authors: Gamal Adel, Shrichand Bhuria, Alessandro Catalano, Liber Dorizzi, Leonardo Federici, Theodora Moldovan, Bern\'e Nortier, Chara Deanna Punzal, Giulia de Meijere, Gerardo I\~niguez
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ego networks capture the variety of structural patterns in the social interactions of individuals. Recently it has been shown that ego networks in online settings display universal patterns of tie strength distributions, but it is unclear how constraints such as spatial proximity and bounded social bandwidth affect such generic behaviour in offline settings. Here, we analyse the time evolution of interaction activity in ego networks constructed from offline face-to-face and colocation data, compare them to online communication networks, and explore simple cumulative advantage models that capture the varying preferentiality of individuals for specific social ties. We find that patterns of preferentiality at the population level are similar for online and face-to-face networks, but not for colocation data, suggesting that the latter is a poor proxy of social network structure. We also provide evidence that empirical ego networks exhibit a bandwidth in the way communication events are allocated across connections. A model implementing this notion uncovers evidence of universal scaling between the tie preferentiality and bandwidth of individuals, common to all online and offline systems explored. Our findings strengthen our understanding of the fundamental mechanisms governing human communication and help disentangle the internal and external factors shaping tie evolution across social contexts.
tldr: This paper studies tie strength dynamics in online and offline ego networks using cumulative advantage models.
motivation: To understand how spatial proximity and social bandwidth affect tie activity patterns across different social contexts.
method: Analyzes face-to-face, colocation, and online communication datasets, and fits cumulative advantage models with preferentiality and bandwidth parameters.
result: Preferentiality patterns are similar for online and face-to-face networks but not colocation; a universal scaling between preferentiality and bandwidth is found.
conclusion: The findings reveal fundamental mechanisms of human communication and the role of constraints in tie evolution.

title: Students Using GenAI Lag Behind In Problem-solving Competence: An Agent-based Study Of Classroom Networks
authors: Lorenzo Betti, Iacopo Caporossi, Carsten K\"allner, Karolina Levanait\.e, Chenyu Li, Xuan-Chen Liu, Giulia Lorenzini, Vittoria Socci, Michele Re Fiorentin, Ilaria Stanzani, Marta Baratto
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The development of problem-solving competence (PSC) among high school students is foundational for preparing resilient and adaptive citizens. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can support this process, but it may also encourage students to offload part of the cognitive work that is necessary for deep learning. While the individual effects of GenAI use are increasingly studied, its collective consequences for competence development within classroom environments remain underexplored. In this study, we use an agent-based model to simulate the evolution of PSC in a high school physics classroom, where students complete tasks individually, in collaboration with peers, or with the support of GenAI. By comparing classrooms with and without access to GenAI across different peer-network structures, we show that GenAI use can diminish competence development and increase the share of students remaining in lower competence tiers. These results suggest that the educational impact of GenAI should be assessed not only through individual learning outcomes but also through its effects on collective competence dynamics.
tldr: This paper uses an agent-based model to study how GenAI use affects problem-solving competence development in high school physics classrooms.
motivation: To understand the collective impact of GenAI on student competence development beyond individual effects.
method: Agent-based simulation of classroom networks comparing scenarios with and without GenAI access across different peer structures.
result: GenAI use diminishes competence development and increases the proportion of students in lower competence tiers.
conclusion: Educational impact of GenAI should be assessed through collective competence dynamics, not just individual outcomes.

title: From Streaks To Synergies: A Multi-scale Analysis Of Performance And Scoring In The Nba
authors: Malvina Bozhidarova, Yanpei Cai, Ricardo M. S. Carvalho, Daniele Cirulli, Quentin Dehaene, Martin Diaz, Alexandra Krasnokutskaya, Bernardo Pereira, Onkar Sadekar, Federico Battiston
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern play-by-play data make it possible to test long-standing intuitions about basketball with the same statistical rigour now routinely applied to other professional sports. Using play-by-play data from 7,054 regular-season and 504 playoff NBA games spanning the 2020-2025 seasons, we provide quantitative insights into scoring patterns and the performance of individual players and teams through methods from statistics, network science, and complexity science. Our findings offer an evidence-based perspective on in-season and in-game performance that can inform coaching strategies, player evaluation, and tactical decision-making.
tldr: This paper analyzes NBA basketball scoring patterns and player/team performance using play-by-play data and methods from statistics, network science, and complexity science.
motivation: To provide quantitative insights into long-standing intuitions about basketball performance and scoring.
method: Applied statistical, network science, and complexity science methods to play-by-play data from 7,054 regular-season and 504 playoff NBA games (2020-2025).
result: Offers evidence-based perspectives on in-season and in-game performance.
conclusion: Findings can inform coaching strategies, player evaluation, and tactical decision-making.

title: SimPol: Simulating Polarisation In Political Belief Networks In European Countries
authors: Isabela Burattini Freire, Hongryol Cha, Irina Epure, Sara Filippini, Karan K. H. Manjunatha, Chethan Kavaraganahalli Prasanna, Ivan Samoylenko, Niels van Santen, Adarsh Prabhakaran, Guillermo Romero Moreno
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27968v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Here we combine empirical network analysis with agent-based modelling to understand how different ways of structuring belief systems may affect the polarisation drive, and how the diversity of belief systems in Europe may result in different polarisation trajectories. Using the 2016 European Social Survey, we infer belief networks across 23 European countries via a Bayesian algorithm, revealing that belief systems are predominantly organised around immigration, LGBT rights, and economic interventionism, reflecting the influence of populist discourse across the continent. We further verify a Western-Eastern divide across the national belief networks: in Western European countries, left-right self-identification is a more reliable predictor of broader belief alignment, whereas in Eastern Europe this relationship breaks down. By applying these empirical belief networks into a sociologically grounded agent-based model, we further show that polarisation is amplified by high individual belief rigidity and low susceptibility to social influence, and that cross-country differences in polarisation levels mirror the same geographic divide observed in belief network topology. These findings establish belief networks topologies as a structural driver of political polarisation, with implications for understanding and anticipating polarisation dynamics across diverse European contexts. We find that populations are not polarised when little attention is placed on maintaining internal coherence and polarisation levels are moderate when high attention is placed in both keeping internal coherence and agreement in beliefs with others.
tldr: This paper uses network analysis and agent-based modeling to study political belief systems and polarization across European countries, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how belief network structures influence political polarization and how these dynamics vary across Europe.
method: They infer belief networks from the 2016 European Social Survey using a Bayesian algorithm and simulate polarization with an agent-based model incorporating belief rigidity and social influence.
result: Belief systems are organized around immigration, LGBT rights, and economic interventionism; a Western-Eastern divide exists in how left-right self-identification predicts belief alignment; polarization is amplified by high belief rigidity and low social influence.
conclusion: Belief network topologies are a structural driver of political polarization, and cross-country differences mirror geographic divides.

title: A Finite Element Method For Fluctuating Navier--Stokes Equations
authors: Dimitrios Gourzoulidis, Mirko Gallo, Soumaya Elkantassi, Toby Kay, Serafim Kalliadasis
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27972v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a finite-element framework for simulating thermal fluctuations in compressible fluids governed by the fluctuating Navier-Stokes equations. The method is designed to preserve the fundamental fluctuation-dissipation balance at the discrete level. This is achieved by defining the stochastic forcing term in the weak formulation, ensuring its covariance is proportional to the discrete viscous dissipation operator. A nodal quadrature rule is employed to eliminate unphysical mesh-scale correlations. The time integration is performed using the Crank-Nicolson scheme to maintain numerical stability and accuracy. The proposed approach is numerically validated in one, two, and three spatial dimensions, demonstrating its capability to correctly capture equilibrium fluctuation statistics across various discretisation parameters.
tldr: This paper develops a finite element method for simulating thermal fluctuations in compressible fluids using the fluctuating Navier-Stokes equations.
motivation: To accurately model thermal fluctuations in fluid dynamics while preserving fluctuation-dissipation balance at the discrete level.
method: The stochastic forcing term is defined in the weak formulation with covariance proportional to the discrete viscous dissipation operator, and a nodal quadrature rule eliminates mesh-scale correlations; time integration uses the Crank-Nicolson scheme.
result: Numerical validation in 1D, 2D, and 3D shows correct equilibrium fluctuation statistics across various discretization parameters.
conclusion: The proposed finite element framework successfully captures thermal fluctuations in compressible fluids, maintaining fluctuation-dissipation balance.

title: $2$-rotundity Of Some Nonseparable Abstract Interpolation Spaces
authors: Denka Kutzarova Stephen Dilworth
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27473v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generalizing a construction due to Argyros and Motakis , we define a nonseparable abstract interpolation space associated to any given reflexive space with an unconditional basis together with the Schreier spaces associated to an increasing sequence of compact families of finite subsets of an uncountable set. Under a mild complexity assumption on the families, we prove that the interpolation space admits a [MATH]-rotund norm with an uncountable [MATH]-unconditional basis.
tldr: The paper studies 2-rotund norms on nonseparable abstract interpolation spaces, a topic in functional analysis with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To generalize a construction by Argyros and Motakis to define nonseparable interpolation spaces with 2-rotund norms.
method: Defines an abstract interpolation space associated to a reflexive space with unconditional basis and Schreier spaces, then proves existence of a 2-rotund norm under mild complexity assumptions.
result: The interpolation space admits a 2-rotund norm with an uncountable unconditional basis.
conclusion: The result extends known renorming techniques to a broader class of nonseparable spaces.

title: Korovkin Type Theorems For Operators Acting On Functions Of Polynomial And Exponential Growth On $[0,\infty)$
authors: Ulrich Abel, Ana-Maria Acu, Margareta Heilmann, Ioan Rasa
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27517v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove two Korovkin-type approximation theorems for sequences of positive linear operators acting on continuous functions on [MATH]. Under the assumption of pointwise convergence on suitable test functions, we establish pointwise convergence for all functions with polynomial or exponential growth. As direct applications, we obtain convergence results for the classical Baskakov and Sz\'asz--Mirakjan operators. The proposed method offers an elementary framework that can be applied to a broad class of positive linear operators.
tldr: This paper proves Korovkin-type approximation theorems for positive linear operators on functions with polynomial or exponential growth on [0,∞).
motivation: To extend classical Korovkin theorems to function spaces with unbounded growth, enabling convergence results for operators like Baskakov and Szász-Mirakjan.
method: The authors develop an elementary framework using pointwise convergence on test functions to establish convergence for all functions with polynomial or exponential growth.
result: They obtain Korovkin-type theorems for functions with polynomial or exponential growth and apply them to classical Baskakov and Szász-Mirakjan operators.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a simple, broadly applicable framework for proving convergence of positive linear operators on unbounded domains.

title: Continuous Diffraction Spectrum And The Uniform Vanishing Of Fourier--Bohr Coefficients
authors: Nicolae Strungaru
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27553v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we review the connection among continuity of the diffraction spectrum, the (uniform) vanishing of the Fourier--Bohr coefficients and the so called consistent phase frequency.
tldr: The paper reviews the connection between continuity of diffraction spectrum and vanishing of Fourier-Bohr coefficients in the context of aperiodic order.
motivation: To understand the relationship between diffraction properties and Fourier-Bohr coefficients for aperiodic structures.
method: Review and theoretical analysis of existing results on diffraction spectra and Fourier-Bohr coefficients.
result: Establishes that continuous diffraction spectrum implies uniform vanishing of Fourier-Bohr coefficients, and discusses consistent phase frequency.
conclusion: The findings clarify the mathematical structure of diffraction from aperiodic systems.

title: On Strongly Quasiconvex Pseudomonotone Equilibrium Problems In Hadamard Spaces
authors: Nicholas Pischke Luisa Marie Despr\'es
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study two proximal point type methods for finding equilibrium points of pseudomonotone and strongly quasiconvex bifunctions. Extending results by A. Iusem and F. Lara, we prove the strong convergence of these methods over general complete geodesic metric spaces of nonpositive curvature, so-called Hadamard spaces. Our arguments are quite elementary and in particular effective, yielding sublinear non-asymptotic guarantees for the distance of the iterates towards the solution. These quantitative results are novel even in the context of Euclidean spaces, the original setting of the work by Iusem and Lara, and the simplicity of our arguments allows us to either weaken or even fully discharge various assumptions featuring in this previous work. We also provide an existence result for solutions of equilibrium problems generated by suitably semicontinuous, pseudomonotone and strongly quasiconvex bifunctions over general Hadamard spaces, and derive from this that every lower-semicontinuous strongly quasiconvex function over a Hadamard space has a minimizer, answering a question of the second author.
tldr: This paper studies proximal point methods for equilibrium problems in Hadamard spaces, focusing on pseudomonotone and strongly quasiconvex bifunctions.
motivation: To extend convergence results for equilibrium problems from Euclidean spaces to general Hadamard spaces and to weaken assumptions.
method: Proposes two proximal point type methods and proves strong convergence using elementary arguments, yielding sublinear non-asymptotic guarantees.
result: Establishes strong convergence with sublinear rates, weakens assumptions from prior work, and provides an existence result for solutions of equilibrium problems in Hadamard spaces.
conclusion: The methods are effective in Hadamard spaces, and the results answer an open question about minimizers of strongly quasiconvex functions.

title: Uncertainty-aware Power System Planning Via Gradient Descent
authors: Robert Mieth Mehrnoush Ghazanfariharandi
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Power system planning models provide important guidance on long-term investment strategies with significant socio-economic impact. To remain computationally manageable, however, such planning models compromise on the level of complexity with which power system operations and physics are captured. A common approach in most planning models is to collapse multi-stage power system operational processes into a single stage and, as a result, give up on the ability to account for uncertainty in each operational stage. In light of newly emerging load patterns and the continuing adoption of weather-dependent stochastic renewable generation, this uncertainty, however, becomes increasingly impactful on operations, and ignoring it has been shown to cause underinvestment in transmission capacity and flexible resources. In this work, we present a computational approach for power system expansion planning that explicitly considers two-stage day-ahead (DA) and real-time (RT) operational decisions under uncertainty while retaining time-coupling constraints to allow modeling generator ramping and energy storage. To solve the resulting optimization problem efficiently, we employ a projected stochastic gradient descent algorithm combined with a primal-dual optimization framework and an exponential moving average smoothing strategy to improve convergence stability. We evaluate the resulting investment decisions within a two-stage DA and RT simulation framework and compare them with a classic expansion planning model that assumes perfect knowledge of renewable generation. Our experiments show that the proposed framework achieves lower total system costs while ensuring that the implemented technology portfolio achieves set renewable integration targets.
tldr: This paper presents a gradient-descent-based optimization framework for power system expansion planning under operational uncertainty.
motivation: Traditional power system planning models collapse multi-stage operations into a single stage, ignoring uncertainty in day-ahead and real-time decisions, leading to underinvestment in transmission and flexible resources.
method: The authors formulate a two-stage stochastic optimization problem with time-coupling constraints and solve it using a projected stochastic gradient descent algorithm with primal-dual framework and exponential moving average smoothing.
result: The proposed framework achieves lower total system costs compared to classic planning models that assume perfect renewable generation knowledge, while meeting renewable integration targets.
conclusion: Explicitly modeling two-stage operational uncertainty in planning can improve investment decisions and reduce costs.

title: Policy Gradient Learning For Distributionally Robust Markov Decision Processes Under Wasserstein Ambiguity
authors: Yadh Hafsi, Samy Mekkaoui, Huy\^en Pham, Kaixin Yan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study finite-horizon Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) under distributional uncertainty in the transition kernels and develop a policy-gradient framework for Wasserstein distributionally robust control. Ambiguity is modeled by state-action dependent Wasserstein balls around nominal transition kernels, leading to a max-min control problem over randomized policies and admissible transition laws. Since the worst-case transition law depends implicitly on the policy parameters, the usual policy-gradient argument does not apply. We address this difficulty by using a Wasserstein dual reformulation of the robust Bellman recursion and analyzing its directional differentiability. This yields an explicit recursive characterization of the robust policy gradient. Building on this characterization, we propose a robust actor-critic algorithm and illustrate its behavior on discrete and continuous benchmark examples.
tldr: This paper develops a policy gradient algorithm for distributionally robust Markov decision processes under Wasserstein ambiguity.
motivation: To handle uncertainty in transition kernels in MDPs, which is common in real-world applications where the true dynamics are unknown.
method: Uses a Wasserstein dual reformulation of the robust Bellman recursion and analyzes its directional differentiability to derive an explicit robust policy gradient, then proposes a robust actor-critic algorithm.
result: Provides a recursive characterization of the robust policy gradient and demonstrates the algorithm on discrete and continuous benchmark examples.
conclusion: The proposed method enables efficient policy optimization under distributional uncertainty in MDPs.

title: Multidimensional Quadratic BSDEs With Weak Interactions And Their Applications In Mean-field Games Of Controls
authors: Ulrich Horst, Emil Schmidek, Huilin Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The well-posedness of multidimensional quadratic backward stochastic differential equations (qBSDEs) remains one of the central open problems in BSDE theory. Motivated by a mean-field utility maximization model with price impact, we introduce a new class of multidimensional qBSDEs that lies beyond the scope of existing well-posedness results (see (2.15) for the generator). In order to study the limit as the number of players tends to infinity, we establish existence and uniqueness for a large class of such qBSDEs under suitable smallness conditions imposed on each individual dynamics. A key feature of our approach is that the smallness condition is independent of the dimension of the BSDE system. In particular, the system itself is not confined to a small neighborhood, which allows us to analyze the mean-field limit of the underlying utility maximization problem. Such a condition is also natural in view of the well-known fact that general multidimensional qBSDEs may fail to admit solutions in the absence of suitable smallness assumptions. In addition, we derive a stability result for this class of equations based on the application of Picard iterations. Finally, using this stability result, we establish quantitative convergence rates toward the corresponding mean-field equilibria in two settings: Nash and Radner equilibria.
tldr: The paper proves well-posedness for a class of multidimensional quadratic BSDEs with weak interactions and applies them to mean-field games of controls.
motivation: Multidimensional quadratic BSDEs are a central open problem; the authors are motivated by a mean-field utility maximization model with price impact.
method: They introduce a new class of qBSDEs and establish existence and uniqueness under smallness conditions independent of dimension, using Picard iterations and stability results.
result: They prove well-posedness and derive quantitative convergence rates toward mean-field equilibria for Nash and Radner equilibria.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous framework for analyzing mean-field games of controls with weak interactions, extending BSDE theory.

title: A Backstepping Framework For Unconstrained Accelerated Optimization Algorithms
authors: Song Chen, Jiaxu Liu, Chao Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper introduces a control-theoretic perspective on unconstrained optimization algorithms using the backstepping methods. We model the optimization process as an augmented strict-feedback system given by [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], with a regulated output [MATH]. This formulation recasts the development of unconstrained optimization algorithms as a feedback control problem, where the goal is to design the input [MATH] to ensure [MATH]. By employing backstepping, we recursively synthesize the actual feedback law [MATH] after initially selecting a virtual control for [MATH]. For convex objective functions, we develop a general synthesis framework for augmented strict-feedback systems and specialize it to the standard strict-feedback case. This unified framework successfully recovers the constant-parameter Nesterov flow and the proportional-integral-derivative (PID) accelerated optimizer as direct corollaries. We further establish that, given a fixed virtual control, the universal second-step law is inverse optimal with respect to an induced outer-tracking problem. This reveals that the optimality of the control law is conditionally dependent on the target manifold prescribed by the virtual control, rather than holding globally across all possible backstepping designs. Finally, we formulate a formal optimal-backstepping theorem that elevates this optimality principle to the virtual-control stage by solving a reduced Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman problem. These contributions collectively yield a robust and general backstepping-driven paradigm for the analysis and design of continuous-time unconstrained optimization algorithms.
tldr: This paper applies control-theoretic backstepping methods to design continuous-time unconstrained optimization algorithms, recovering known accelerated flows and establishing inverse optimality.
motivation: To provide a unified control-theoretic framework for designing and analyzing accelerated optimization algorithms, leveraging backstepping to systematically construct feedback laws.
method: Models optimization as an augmented strict-feedback system and recursively synthesizes control laws via backstepping, then analyzes inverse optimality and solves a reduced Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman problem.
result: Recovers constant-parameter Nesterov flow and PID accelerated optimizer as special cases; proves that the second-step law is inverse optimal conditioned on the virtual control; formulates an optimal-backstepping theorem.
conclusion: The backstepping paradigm offers a robust and general approach for continuous-time unconstrained optimization algorithm design, with conditional optimality properties.

title: hp-Optimal Dg Approximation And Robust Schwarz Decompositions On One-Irregular Cubical Meshes
authors: Weiying Zheng Situan Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study hp approximation and additive Schwarz decompositions for variable-order cubical finite element spaces on one-irregular meshes. For fitted homogeneous diffusion interface problems on one-irregular hexahedral meshes, we prove an hp-optimal energy-norm estimate for the interior penalty DG method. The interpolation input is a conforming hp interpolant obtained from fitted conforming closures of one-irregular vertex patches. We also derive stable decompositions for conforming and DG spaces. On one-irregular quadrilateral meshes the bounds allow locally comparable variable polynomial degrees and are independent of the mesh size, the local degrees, and, under a local coefficient quasi-monotonicity condition, the coefficient contrast. On one-irregular hexahedral meshes the conforming decomposition has the corresponding polylogarithmic loss; the DG-to-conforming reduction is used there for uniform-degree DG spaces. Numerical experiments illustrate the p-optimal DG error estimate and the robustness of the DG Schwarz preconditioner.
tldr: This paper presents hp-optimal discontinuous Galerkin approximations and robust Schwarz decompositions for elliptic interface problems on one-irregular cubical meshes.
motivation: To develop efficient and robust numerical methods for solving partial differential equations with discontinuous coefficients on non-conforming meshes.
method: The authors construct conforming hp interpolants on one-irregular vertex patches and derive stable additive Schwarz decompositions for both conforming and DG spaces, with polylogarithmic losses in 3D.
result: They prove hp-optimal energy-norm error estimates for the interior penalty DG method and demonstrate robustness of the DG Schwarz preconditioner with respect to mesh size, polynomial degree, and coefficient contrast.
conclusion: The proposed DG approximation and preconditioner achieve optimal convergence rates and robustness, validated by numerical experiments.

title: A Dynamical Low-rank Multilevel Monte Carlo Estimator For High-Dimensional Kinetic Equations
authors: Chinmay Patwardhan, Sebastian Krumscheid, Jonas Kusch, Emil L{\o}vbak, Pia Stammer
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27888v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kinetic equations are used to model a wide range of phenomena important for real-world applications. Their applications span astrophysics, nuclear physics, engineering, and social sciences. Due to their high-dimensional phase space, modelling and quantifying uncertainties, relevant for applications, poses a significant challenge even for modern computing infrastructure. In recent years, dynamical low-rank approximation (DLRA) has gained popularity for making fine grid simulations of high-dimensional problems feasible by evolving the solution of a time-dependent PDE as a low-rank factorization. This reduces the computational and memory requirements significantly. In this work, we propose a low-rank multilevel Monte Carlo estimator for kinetic equations based on a probabilistic rank-adaptive DLRA time integrator. The level hierarchy of the low-rank multilevel estimator is constructed through spatial refinement and by ensuring that the low-rank error remains below the spatial discretization error. We demonstrate the efficacy of the estimator through several numerical experiments from radiation transport, radiation therapy, and shallow water flow.
tldr: This paper proposes a dynamical low-rank multilevel Monte Carlo estimator for high-dimensional kinetic equations, focusing on computational efficiency for uncertainty quantification.
motivation: Kinetic equations have high-dimensional phase spaces, making uncertainty quantification computationally expensive. Existing methods like DLRA reduce cost but lack efficient uncertainty propagation.
method: The authors develop a probabilistic rank-adaptive DLRA time integrator and construct a multilevel Monte Carlo estimator where the level hierarchy is based on spatial refinement and low-rank error control.
result: Numerical experiments in radiation transport, radiation therapy, and shallow water flow demonstrate the estimator's efficacy in reducing computational cost while maintaining accuracy.
conclusion: The proposed low-rank multilevel Monte Carlo estimator enables feasible uncertainty quantification for high-dimensional kinetic equations, with potential applications in various fields.

title: Optimal Estimators For Heavy-Tailed Mean Estimation Via Convex Analysis
authors: Bert Zwart Bart P. G. van Parys
abstract: ArXiv:2606.27899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study optimal estimation of the location parameter of a distribution known only to lie in a symmetric moment class [MATH]: the mean-zero distributions with bounded moment [MATH] for a fixed even [MATH]. Our main result concerns the fixed-margin regime, where the error margin [MATH] is fixed as [MATH]: we give an exact large-deviation characterization of the smallest worst-case probability [MATH] of an error exceeding [MATH] that any measurable estimator can guarantee with [MATH] observations. Its exponential rate is exactly a two-point Hellinger exponent over the class shifted to means [MATH], [MATH], achieved non-asymptotically, [MATH], by a monotone [MATH]-estimator synthesized from a two-parameter convex program. Lagrangian duality collapses the infinite-dimensional search over estimating functions to two multipliers, which determine a pair of envelopes characterizing the optimal estimating functions; the sandwich shape posited ad hoc in prior constructions emerges naturally. For bounded variance ([MATH], [MATH]) the exponent is [MATH]. In the fixed-confidence regime, holding [MATH] fixed and letting the optimal margin [MATH] shrink with [MATH], the same synthesis stays optimal to leading order for several concrete classes. As [MATH] it attains the sharp constant [MATH] of Catoni for bounded variance and the constant [MATH] of Lee and Bhatt et al. for bounded [MATH]-moments, [MATH], thereby shown tight; for slowly varying [MATH] it is leading-order minimax at every fixed [MATH]. The least-favorable distributions are simple, supported on at most three atoms.
tldr: This paper studies optimal mean estimation for heavy-tailed distributions using convex analysis and large deviation theory.
motivation: Heavy-tailed distributions pose challenges for classical mean estimators; the authors aim to find minimax optimal estimators with tight error bounds.
method: They formulate the problem as a convex optimization over estimating functions, use Lagrangian duality to reduce to two multipliers, and derive optimal estimators via a two-parameter convex program.
result: They provide exact large-deviation characterizations of the worst-case error probability, achieving optimal exponential rates and sharp constants for bounded variance and bounded moment classes.
conclusion: The proposed monotone M-estimators are asymptotically optimal and achieve leading-order minimax performance for fixed confidence and fixed margin regimes.

title: A Primal-dual Splitting Algorithm For Monotone Inclusions With Applications
authors: Changchi Huang, Jigen Peng, Liqian Qin, Yuchao Tang
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a broad class of structured monotone inclusion problems in real Hilbert spaces. We propose a novel primal-dual splitting algorithm for solving such inclusions, which accommodates multiple monotone operators and cocoercive terms, as well as a composite monotone operator involving the linear map. The algorithm combines forward evaluations for the cocoercive components with backward resolvent steps for the monotone operators and employs a dual update for the linear composition term. It generalizes and unifies several existing methods, while requiring only a single resolvent or operator evaluation per iteration. We prove weak convergence of the iterates under standard assumptions on monotonicity and cocoercivity. Furthermore, we establish strong convergence under a mild regularity condition, such as uniform monotonicity. Numerical experiments on image deblurring and denoising problems demonstrate the efficiency and flexibility of the proposed algorithm.
tldr: This paper proposes a primal-dual splitting algorithm for solving monotone inclusion problems in Hilbert spaces, with applications to image processing.
motivation: To develop a unified and efficient algorithm for a broad class of structured monotone inclusion problems that arise in optimization and image processing.
method: The algorithm combines forward evaluations for cocoercive operators with backward resolvent steps for monotone operators and a dual update for the linear composition term, requiring only one resolvent or operator evaluation per iteration.
result: Weak convergence of iterates is proved under standard assumptions, and strong convergence is established under uniform monotonicity. Numerical experiments on image deblurring and denoising demonstrate efficiency.
conclusion: The proposed algorithm generalizes and unifies several existing methods and is effective for image restoration tasks.

title: A Robust Mixed Finite Element Formulation For Third Medium Contact
authors: M. Vorwerk, J. Schr\"oder, P. Wriggers
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Third medium contact provides a smooth continuum alternative to classical contact algorithms by replacing explicit contact constraints with a highly compliant fictitious medium. In this work, an auxiliary-field stabilization is introduced in which a deformation-gradient-like field is treated as an independent unknown in the third medium and coupled to the physical deformation gradient by a penalty term. A gradient contribution acting on the auxiliary field provides the regularization mechanism without requiring a direct evaluation of higher displacement derivatives. Linear and quadratic interpolation spaces are investigated, including continuous and element-wise discontinuous auxiliary-field approximations. The numerical results show that continuous low-order auxiliary fields provide an effective gradient-type stabilization of the third medium, even when the displacement field is approximated by first-order finite elements. For element-wise discontinuous auxiliary fields, the additional unknowns remain local to each element and can be eliminated locally by static condensation, so that the global system does not necessarily contain additional auxiliary degrees of freedom. Benchmark problems involving large deformation, progressive self-contact and severe third-medium compression are used to assess the formulation.
tldr: This paper presents a finite element formulation for third medium contact, a computational mechanics method for simulating contact between deformable bodies.
motivation: Classical contact algorithms often involve explicit constraints that can be numerically challenging; third medium contact offers a smooth alternative by replacing constraints with a compliant fictitious medium.
method: An auxiliary-field stabilization is introduced where a deformation-gradient-like field is treated as an independent unknown in the third medium, coupled to the physical deformation gradient via a penalty term, with gradient regularization acting on the auxiliary field.
result: Continuous low-order auxiliary fields provide effective gradient-type stabilization even with first-order finite elements; element-wise discontinuous auxiliary fields can be eliminated locally by static condensation.
conclusion: The proposed formulation effectively handles large deformation, progressive self-contact, and severe third-medium compression, demonstrating robustness in benchmark problems.

title: High-Order Asymptotic-Preserving Schemes For Kinetic Equations From Rarefied To Incompressible Regimes
authors: Giacomo Dimarco, Axel Klar, Theresa K\"ofler, Lorenzo Pareschi, Tiwari Sudarshan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28040v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work introduces a novel high-order numerical framework for solving kinetic equations, designed to remain uniformly valid across all regimes of the mean free path, spanning from the rarefied kinetic scale to the incompressible hydrodynamic limit. The method is built upon a micro-macro decomposition, which reformulates the underlying kinetic equation into a coupled system consisting of a macroscopic part, representing the fluid-dynamic evolution, and a microscopic part, describing the non-equilibrium deviations. The proposed framework ensures high-order temporal accuracy through the use of Implicit-Explicit Runge-Kutta methods, which provide stability and efficiency in stiff regimes, while spatial resolution is enhanced by combining finite-difference WENO reconstructions with high-order central difference approximations. A key feature of the proposed methodology is its Asymptotic-Preserving (AP) property. We demonstrate that, in the appropriate asymptotic limit as the mean free path tends to zero, the scheme consistently reduces to a high-order finite-difference formulation of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. To support the theoretical findings, a set of numerical experiments are performed on one- and two-dimensional benchmark problems, which confirm the accuracy, stability, and versatility of the method across different flow regimes.
tldr: This paper develops high-order asymptotic-preserving numerical schemes for kinetic equations, targeting fluid dynamics across rarefied to incompressible regimes.
motivation: Kinetic equations are computationally challenging across different mean free path regimes; existing schemes lack high-order accuracy and uniform validity.
method: The method uses micro-macro decomposition to split the equation into macroscopic fluid and microscopic non-equilibrium parts, combined with Implicit-Explicit Runge-Kutta for time integration and WENO/finite-difference for spatial discretization.
result: The scheme achieves high-order accuracy and preserves the asymptotic limit to incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, validated on 1D and 2D benchmarks.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides an accurate and stable numerical tool for multiscale kinetic problems, with potential extensions to more complex models.

title: Global Convergence Analysis Of Mixtures Of Exponential Densities
authors: Kathryn Dullerud Rajita Chandak
abstract: ArXiv:2606.28053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The theoretical foundations of the EM algorithm are often thought of in the context of Gaussian mixture models, However, the practical use cases of the EM algorithm span beyond Gaussian models. This paper establishes the first step towards understanding the behavior of the EM algorithm under mixtures of non-Gaussian densities. We show that a mixture of two Exponential distributions can be approximated by the EM algorithm at the sub-Exponential rate of convergence in at most [MATH] iterations. The results here show that extending away from Gaussian mixture models does not affect the statistical performance of the EM algorithm. Furthermore, we present generalizations of typical assumptions in the Gaussian setting like minimum mean-separation and signal-to-noise ratio to the sub-Exponential setting. A simulation study is used to highlight the empirical performance of EM for mixtures of exponentials with promising results for the extension of existing theory to a larger class of mixture models.
tldr: This paper analyzes the convergence of the EM algorithm for mixtures of exponential distributions, extending theory beyond Gaussian mixtures.
motivation: The EM algorithm is widely used for Gaussian mixtures, but its theoretical behavior for non-Gaussian mixtures is less understood. This work aims to establish convergence guarantees for exponential mixtures.
method: The authors prove sub-exponential convergence rates for the EM algorithm on mixtures of two exponential distributions, generalizing assumptions like minimum mean-separation and signal-to-noise ratio to the sub-exponential setting.
result: The EM algorithm converges at a sub-exponential rate in at most a specified number of iterations, and simulation studies confirm empirical performance.
conclusion: Extending EM theory to non-Gaussian mixtures does not degrade statistical performance, suggesting broader applicability of existing convergence results.

title: Fractional Quadratic Obstructions To The Local Controllability Of The Burgers Equation
authors: Thomas Perrin
